A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe the same UniMRG study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on three UMM architectures, quantitative and qualitative ablations, and out-of-distribution depth-generation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised OpenUni GenEval results in Tables 1 and 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the four-task objective, unit loss weights, encoder-freezing rules, and inference procedure. OpenUni's additional pixel-generation training stage already exists in v1; its revised duration is a budget change.

E1.justification: Both use LLaVA Mix-665K and LLaVA-Next-Data, the same seven understanding/generation benchmarks, and the MidjourneyV6 out-of-distribution depth-generation scenario. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Base, SFT, and RecA comparisons for all three architectures; Table 2 retains the same comparison models. Newly cited works are not added to the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 changes OpenUni's additional pixel-generation stage from 2,000 to 3,000 steps, retaining its initial 2,000-step training stage. This is a localized reported budget revision; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or the earlier specification was corrected.

E4.justification: The cumulative loss ablations in Table 3, qualitative ablations in Figure 5, 1,000-image MidjourneyV6 analysis in Figure 6, and representation-generation examples in Appendix C remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 4 replace OpenUni GenEval totals: Base 50.97 to 61.13, SFT 38.07 to 46.03, RecA 58.01 to 70.07, and UniMRG 55.82 to 68.00. Category scores and some category winners also change, while overall ordering remains. Updates are confined to this architecture/benchmark block; other metrics and architectures retain their results. These replacements do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Section 3 loss equations, Appendix A formulations of autoregressive, diffusion, and masked-autoregressive modeling, and Appendix B depth-normalization formula are unchanged. No theoretical result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: architecture-agnostic intrinsic-representation generation improves perception, hallucination mitigation, spatial understanding, and generation. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.4 and Appendix C retain the geometric/structural mechanism explanations, interpretation of generalization, and Show-o codebook-bottleneck limitation. Future extensions and the impact discussion are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 revises the disclosed OpenUni pixel-generation stage length from 2,000 to 3,000 steps. The remaining optimizer, learning-rate, batching, preprocessing, prompt, hardware, and runtime information is retained.

R1.justification: Six introductory citations are added, including DiverseGRPO, Safe-Sora, model merging, and translator-guided geometric perception. Sections 2 and 3.2 retain the substantive positioning relative to prior work.

P1.justification: Limited edits replace introductory task examples with citations, expand affiliation and correspondence information, add acknowledgments, and shorten the segmentation-prompt heading in Appendix B.4. The scientific narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The expanded first-page affiliation block and conference footer alter the layout, with the Introduction moving to the right column and subsequent text and references reflowing. All seven figures and four tables retain their artwork or structural design.

improvement.justification: Tables 1 and 4 revise OpenUni GenEval scores, including the base model and comparators, without explaining why. Appendix B.1 also increases the reported training budget. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether these updates correct earlier reporting or reflect changed experiments, limiting assessment of their quality benefit. The method and remaining evidence are stable, while citation and presentation edits provide no decisive net improvement or deterioration.
